newsitem.title: USA: Eurobond market will rival US Treasuries - expert.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond market will rival US Treasuries - expert.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury bond market may run into some stiff competition as the idea of a united European bond market matures, John Meehan, managing director for fixed-income at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell warned on Saturday.

"As the Euro bond becomes sound and seasoned, I see some real implications for the U.S. Treasury market," Meehan, 1997 chairman of PSA The Bond Market Trade Association, said during a panel discussion at PSA's 21st annual conference here.

"I think the implications are quite significant, not just for (U.S.) markets, but for the country" as a whole, Meehan said. The U.S. may have to be more disciplined regarding its deficit "because people aren't just going to be jumping in and buying U.S. Treasuries," Meehan said.

Meehan was referring to a 1991 agreement among 12 European nations to set up a European Monetary Union that would mesh markets and set up a single currency, the euro, by 1999. Currently, 15 countries have signed on to all, or part, of the unification process.
"It's the right thing for Europe to do," Meehan said. "(But) over time, it will rival the U.S. Treasuries market," he said.
Meehan said China and other large foreign holders of Treasuries now will have "alternatives that can cause some dislocations in the (U.S. Treasury) market."
"With one currency, I see more blocks of securities moving back and forth," Meehan said. "There will be some choices, but the choices are not so confusing, because we (will) have one currency."
"The World Bank and Fannie Mae and other agencies with access to the book-entry system will be able to issue global bonds with pretty easy access to the settlement process in Europe," Meehan said.
